In [[set theory]], an '''extender''' is a system of [[Ultrafilter (set theory)|ultrafilters]] which represents an [[elementary embedding]] witnessing [[large cardinal]] properties. A nonprincipal ultrafilter is the most basic case of an extender.

A <math>(\kappa, \lambda)</math>-extender can be defined as an elementary embedding of some model <math>M</math> of ZFC<sup>−</sup> (ZFC minus the [[power set axiom]]) having critical point <math>\kappa \in M</math>, and which maps <math>\kappa</math> to an ordinal at least equal to <math>\lambda</math>. It can also be defined as a collection of ultrafilters, one for each <math>n</math>-[[tuple]] drawn from <math>\lambda</math>.

==Formal definition of an extender==

Let &kappa; and &lambda; be cardinals with &kappa;&le;&lambda;. Then, a set <math>E = \{E_a | a\in [\lambda]^{<\omega}\}</math> is called a (κ,λ)-extender if the following properties are satisfied:
# each <math>E_a</math> is a &kappa;-complete nonprincipal ultrafilter on [&kappa;]<sup>&lt;&omega;</sup> and furthermore
## at least one <math>E_a</math> is not &kappa;<sup>+</sup>-complete,
## for each <math>\alpha \in \kappa,</math> at least one <math>E_a</math> contains the set <math>\{s \in [\kappa]^{|a|} : \alpha \in s\}.</math>
# (Coherence) The <math>E_a</math> are coherent (so that the [[ultraproduct|ultrapowers]] Ult(''V'',''E<sub>a</sub>'') form a directed system).
# (Normality) If <math>f</math> is such that <math>\{s \in [\kappa]^{|a|}: f(s) \in \max s\} \in E_a,</math> then for some <math>b \supseteq a,\ \{t \in \kappa^{|b|} : (f \circ \pi_{ba})(t) \in t\} \in E_b.</math>
# (Wellfoundedness) The limit ultrapower Ult(''V'',''E'') is [[axiom of regularity|wellfounded]] (where Ult(''V'',''E'') is the [[direct limit]] of the ultrapowers Ult(''V'',''E<sub>a</sub>'')).

By coherence, one means that if <math>a</math> and <math>b</math> are finite subsets of &lambda; such that <math>b</math> is a superset of <math>a,</math> then if <math>X</math> is an element of the ultrafilter <math>E_b</math> and one chooses the right way to project <math>X</math> down to a set of sequences of length <math>|a|,</math> then <math>X</math> is an element of <math>E_a.</math> More formally, for <math>b = \{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n\},</math> where <math>\alpha_1 < \dots < \alpha_n < \lambda,</math> and <math>a = \{\alpha_{i_1},\dots,\alpha_{i_m}\},</math> where <math>m \leq n</math> and for <math>j \leq m</math> the <math>i_j</math> are pairwise distinct and at most <math>n,</math> we define the projection <math>\pi_{ba} : \{\xi_1, \dots, \xi_n\} \mapsto \{\xi_{i_1}, \dots, \xi_{i_m}\}\ (\xi_1 < \dots < \xi_n).</math>

Then <math>E_a</math> and <math>E_b</math> cohere if
<math display=block>X \in E_a \iff \{s : \pi_{ba}(s) \in X\} \in E_b.</math>

==Defining an extender from an elementary embedding==

Given an elementary embedding <math>j : V \to M,</math> which maps the set-theoretic universe <math>V</math> into a [[Transitive set#Transitive models of set theory|transitive]] [[inner model]] <math>M,</math> with [[critical point (set theory)|critical point]] κ, and a cardinal λ, κ≤λ≤''j''(κ),  one defines <math>E = \{E_a | a \in [\lambda]^{<\omega}\}</math> as follows:
<math display=block>\text{for } a \in [\lambda]^{<\omega}, X \subseteq [\kappa]^{<\omega} : \quad X \in E_a \iff a \in j(X).</math>
One can then show that <math>E</math> has all the properties stated above in the definition and therefore is a (&kappa;,&lambda;)-extender.
